note: Reconstructed by the Veyra team from the public GitHub thread micro_ros_stm32cubemx_utils #139 (what the participants posted, in the order posted). Dates, time and costs were not recorded in the thread summary, so they are left empty. Not an interview.

walkthrough.system: Board Ethernet transport (STM32H7, LwIP, micro-ROS client)
walkthrough.symptom: The micro-ROS agent opens a session with the board and closes it almost at once; the board then keeps sending small packets.
walkthrough.why_ambiguous: The agent log records only what the agent received and sent. It cannot see what the board wrote into its buffer or what went on the wire, so a firmware, network or agent fault all fit it.

steps.check: Inspect in the debugger what the board sends
steps.why: The agent dropped the session right after it was created
steps.decided_by: The debugger showed unexpected data being sent by the board

steps.check: Disable the D-cache (SCB_DisableDCache) and run the session again
steps.why: Unexpected bytes from a buffer the CPU had written point at memory the Ethernet DMA reads
steps.decided_by: With the D-cache disabled the problem was worked around

steps.check: Clean the D-cache (SCB_CleanDCache_by_Addr, 32-byte aligned) on the Tx buffers in low_level_output() of ethernetif.c
steps.why: Keep the D-cache on and make the Tx buffers coherent before the DMA reads them
steps.decided_by: The reporter wrote it was indeed a cache coherence issue; another user reported the patch works on a Nucleo F7

walkthrough.final_cause: Cache coherence in the STM32H7 LwIP Ethernet port: the D-cache was not cleaned before the Ethernet DMA sent a frame, so the agent received zeroed packets (as reported in the thread).
